newsitem.title: USA: EDS reports higher profits, but outlook hits stock. [CORRECTED 19:31 GMT]
newsitem.headline: EDS reports higher profits, but outlook hits stock. [CORRECTED 19:31 GMT]

text.p: Electronic Data Systems Corp. said Wednesday its third quarter earnings and sales increased, but Wall Street hammered its stock in response to a warning of slower growth in the fourth quarter.

Reporting a full quarter's results for the first time since it was spun off in June by General Motors Corp., EDS said new business this year has lagged last year and, coupled with a slowdown in government spending, would pressure its earnings growth in the fourth quarter.
EDS stock fell $11.50 to $48 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

EDS said it earned $266.4 million or 55 cents a share in the third quarter, up from $245.7 million, or 51 cents a share, in the same period of 1995. Sales increased 16.2 percent to $3.57 billion from $3.07 billion.
The profit met Wall Street estimates, which, according to First Call, averaged 55 cents a share.
(Corrects First Call consensus from 63 cents, thus meeting, rather than falling short of estimate).

EDS, the computer services firm founded by billionaire Ross Perot more than 30 years ago, said it obtained $5.37 billion in new business so far this year. That compared with $6.58 billion in new business in the same period of 1995.

EDS also said it had a gross outstanding receivable from Memorex Telex of about $24 million at the end of the third quarter. Memorex Telex Corp. an EDS customer, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Oct. 15 and announced it was seeking to liquidate and sell its U.S. assets.
EDS said it was too early to determine the amount of EDS' recovery, if any, in the bankruptcy proceeding.

For the first nine months, EDS earned $158 million, or 33 cents a share, on revenue of $10.43 billion. A year earlier, EDS earned $669 million, or $1.40 a share, on sales of $8.80 billion. The current-year period included a one-time charge of $850 million, or $1.12 a share, which it described in June as being related to realigning its operations.
